title: 6.10.9 Lab: Win or lose
description: Three balls to clear the wall. Count the bricks left, take a life for every ball that falls out, and end the game when the wall is cleared or the balls run out.

steps.title: Count the bricks
steps.instructions:
The starter is the game from 6.10.8 with three new things. `lives` starts at 3. `state` is `'play'` while the game runs, the state variable of 6.6.7: the starter's `draw()` only moves the paddle and the ball while `state` is `'play'`, and once it is anything else, pressing R calls `startGame()` for a new wall, a new score and three new lives. The lost-ball test has moved into a new function, `checkEnd()`, still as `if (ball.y > 400 + R) serve();`. The words at the top show the score, the bricks left and the lives, and they say `You cleared the wall!` when `state` is `'won'` and `Out of balls.` when it is `'lost'`.

`bricksLeft()` gives back 0 for now. Make it count: two loops over `bricks`, adding 1 to `n` for every cell that is `1`, as in 6.9.11. The words should read `bricks left: 36` and go down as bricks break.
hints: The same two loops as `drawBricks()`, with `if (bricks[r][c] === 1) n += 1;` inside.
`n` starts at 0 and is given back at the end for you.

steps.title: A lost ball costs a life
steps.instructions: In `checkEnd()`, change the lost-ball line so that, when the ball is past the bottom, it takes 1 from `lives`. Then, if `lives` is now 0, set `state` to `'lost'`; otherwise `serve()` again. Run it and miss three times: the third miss stops the game with `Out of balls. Press R`. Then click the canvas so the sketch hears your keys (5.1.13) and press R for a new game.
hints: `if (ball.y > 400 + R) { lives -= 1; ... }`, with an `if` and an `else` inside the braces.

steps.title: Clear the wall to win
steps.instructions: Still in `checkEnd()`, under the lost-ball test: when `bricksLeft()` is 0, set `state` to `'won'`, a change of state driven by a condition, as in 6.6.17. Clear the wall (it takes a while) and the screen says `You cleared the wall! Press R`. To test it faster, change most of the `'#'` in `WALL` to `'.'` so only two or three bricks are left, then put them back.
hints: `draw()` reads `state` on the next frame: once it is not `'play'`, nothing moves.

requirements.title: bricksLeft counts the bricks
requirements.description: Two loops (index or for...of), counting only the cells that hold a brick, and n goes up. Help: 6.9.11 (Lab: A wall of bricks)

requirements.title: A lost ball costs a life
requirements.description: When the ball falls out, lives goes down by 1; at 0 the state becomes 'lost', otherwise the ball is served again. Help: 6.6.7 (Reading: moSHion docs: The state Variable)

requirements.title: A cleared wall wins
requirements.description: When bricksLeft() is 0, the state becomes 'won'. Help: 6.6.17 (Reading: moSHion docs: Condition-Driven Transitions)
